rows.en:
I'm Nozomu Kazama.
I'm a third-year.
Do you all know about 'Kokkuri-san'?
There are all sorts of names for it, like 'Cupid-san' or 'Angel-sama,' but basically they're all the same thing.{p}

You write out the kana syllabary, the words 'yes' and 'no,' and the numbers 0 through 9 on a sheet of paper, and draw a torii gate in the middle.
You put a ten-yen coin on top of that torii, and then two or more people put their index fingers on the coin.
After that, you call Kokkuri-san and ask whatever you want to know.
Then Kokkuri-san graciously answers all sorts of things through that ten-yen coin.
And once you've asked everything you wanted to, you ask Kokkuri-san to kindly go back, and you have to part with the ten-yen coin and the paper right away, either by throwing them out or spending the coin.{p}

Of course, I'm a Kokkuri-san professional, so I've got nothing to worry about.
They have something similar in the West, too.
It's called a 'witch board.'
They even sell special tools made just for it, you know.
Well, I guess things like that are the same all over the world.{p}

...So, the truth is, the third story I'm going to tell is about this Kokkuri-san.
Well, to be precise, it isn't really a story.
Now, now, it'll be way more interesting than some lousy story, I promise.
Listen, and you won't regret it.
Truth is, I can summon Kokkuri-san.
Huh?
You say anybody can summon it?{p}

...How naive.
The Kokkuri-san I summon is the real thing.
I can summon the real Kokkuri-san.
You guys have never seen it, have you?
Heh heh heh... You can even get to see it, you know.
You doubt me, huh?
Well, you'll just have to wait and see.{p}
By the way, {c}{f:|}.{p}Do you believe in Kokkuri-san?
I believe in it
I don't believe in it
I can't say either way

I see, I see.
You're a {f:guy|girl} with real promise.
Believing is what matters.{p}And while we're at it, you also believe that I can summon Kokkuri-san, right?
I believe it
I don't believe it
I can't really say

Wow, you're {f:going to be a big shot|just wonderful}.
You must have some incredible person watching over you as your guardian spirit, don't you?
I can tell.
I can feel a halo shining off you{f:, somehow|, and plenty of it}.{p}

So, I'm thinking of actually doing Kokkuri-san right here, right now. What do you say?
Want to give it a try?{p}I thought I'd tell all sorts of fortunes for you, as a special favor.
I'll try it
I won't
That's the spirit, yeah.{p}

Well, when ordinary people do Kokkuri-san, a lot of the time it's hit or miss, just random.
That's because they often end up calling low-level spirits.
But you see, once you're a Kokkuri-san researcher of my caliber, you've looked into all sorts of things.
I went and discovered a method that's guaranteed to summon a high-level spirit as Kokkuri-san.
First of all, don't be so cheap as to use a ten-yen coin.
You use a 500-yen coin.
That way, you can summon a better Kokkuri-san.{p}
Now, {c}{f:|}.{p}Take out a 500-yen coin, if you please.
Give him a 500-yen coin
Don't give him a 500-yen coin
Say I don't have one on me
Well then, I'm going to use this 500-yen coin to summon Kokkuri-san.

Now, put your index finger on top of this.
...All right, are you ready?{p}

Kokkuri-san, Kokkuri-san.
Please come to us, please come to us.{p}
...And so, Kokkuri-san has arrived.{p}Now, what do you want to ask?
Woman trouble
Money trouble
Studies or work
My future

I see.
So it's about {f:woman|man} trouble, huh?
{f:You|If you}{f:'re quite the perv|want a wonderful boyfriend}, {f:heh heh heh heh...|how about me?}{p}{f:So, right now|By the way}, is there someone you like?
Yes, there is
No, there isn't
{f:I see|Aw, shoot}, so there is someone.{p}And are you going out with that person, maybe?
We're going out
We're not going out

{f:Wow, look at that|Well, I give up}.
You're {f:all hot and bothered|on cloud nine}, huh?{p}
Well then, what shall I divine next?{p}
Woman trouble
Money trouble
Studies or work
My future
I'll stop here

Huh?
You're quitting already?
Even though Kokkuri-san went to the trouble of coming.
What a shame.{p}

Look... the others must be bored, they've started dozing off.
Kokkuri... kokkuri... heads nodding away... there's your Kokkuri-san.{p}

See?
You got to see Kokkuri-san, didn't you?
And that's the end of my story.
Next person, go ahead.
........................
{f:What the heck|What} was that just now?
{f:What was this Kazama guy trying to say?|I wonder what this Kazama person was getting at.}
...Ah!
He went and pocketed the 500-yen coin {f:I|I} gave him!
...What a {f:jerk|creep}!
Shaking down a junior for money like that.
Kazama is looking my way and smiling.
{f:I'll|I'll} just ignore him.
From now on, it'd be best to stay away from this {f:guy|guy}.
I'd better hurry and hear the next person's story.
Next up is...{p}

You don't believe in it, huh?
That's probably because you've never seen anyone who can really summon Kokkuri-san.
Well, just watch.
I'm about to do something amazing for you.{p}

See, this paper.
I use this to summon it.
The real... Kokkuri-san, that is.
And then I'll tell all sorts of fortunes for you.
How about it, want to give it a try?{p}

You're thinking it might be a lie, or it might be true... right?
Then watch closely what I'm about to do.
Right here and now, I'm going to do Kokkuri-san and tell all sorts of fortunes for you.
The Kokkuri-san I do isn't some cheap knockoff like you'd find just anywhere.
Once you've experienced it, I guarantee you'll believe.
How about it, want to give it a try?{p}

What did you say?
You believe in Kokkuri-san, but you don't believe that I can summon it?
I can't forgive that.
{f:That's absolutely unforgivable|This is a serious problem}.
Listen, I can summon the real Kokkuri-san, you know?
I'm the man with the most psychic power of anyone gathered here.{p}If you're going to take that attitude with me, I'll have Kokkuri-san put a curse on you.
Apologize
Don't apologize

Good, as long as you understand.
I'll forgive you. You didn't mean any harm, right?
I like {f:guys|girls} who can honestly apologize when they should.
{f:Guys|Girls} like that have good character, you see.
Besides, I do understand how you feel.
Kokkuri-san exists, but there aren't many people who can really summon it.{p}

...Actions speak louder than words. I'll show you.
To summon the real Kokkuri-san, first you have to carefully select the tool that serves as the medium.
Too difficult? In other words, people use a ten-yen coin to summon Kokkuri-san, right? What I'm saying is, that's actually wrong.
Listen, you use a 500-yen coin.
To summon the real Kokkuri-san, you've got to use a coin worthy of it.
Now watch, I'm about to... Huh?
That's weird.
I was sure I brought a 500-yen coin...
It's not here.
Where did I put it?
...It's gone!
I thought I'd put it in my pocket.
What a pain.
We can't go on like this.
Oh, I know. Hey, you don't happen to have a 500-yen coin, do you?
Without one, I can't summon Kokkuri-san.{p}

I see...
Well then, I'll summon the real Kokkuri-san for you right now.
You can believe after that.
As a special favor, I'll tell all sorts of fortunes for you.{p}

Kazama was looking at me, clearly displeased.
Then, without a word, he took a sheet of paper out of his pocket and set it on the desk.{p}

As he said that, Kazama took out a ten-yen coin, grimy from handling and gone dark brown, and grinned.
This person...
What on earth kind of person was he?
First he said he could summon the real Kokkuri-san, then he said he'd put a curse on me...{p}

"Now, {c}{f:|}, place your finger on the ten-yen coin."
Kazama's words sounded like some kind of sentence being pronounced.
If I had to compare it to something, then...
It was just like a death sentence.
"{c}{f:|}, {f:place your finger on it|put your finger on it}."
Kazama repeated it like someone issuing an absolute command.
{f:I|I} felt strangely like I wanted to cry, and looked around.
He was going to put a curse on {f:me|me}, of all things.
There was no way everyone would just sit there and watch something like this happen.
"{c}{f:|}, hurry and {f:place your finger on it|put your finger on it}."
Kazama grabbed {f:my|my} arm...!{p}

"{f:Stop it!|No!}☆"
{f:I|I} shook his arm off with all my strength.
And then...
Something fell with a faint rustle.{p}

Ah...!
The paper for summoning Kokkuri-san {f:had fallen|had fallen} to the floor.
"Aaah!"
Kazama let out a shout.{p}

"You dropped the ritual paper!
You'll be cursed!
{c}, {f:you|you}... you're going to be cursed...☆"
Everyone in the club room held their breath and stared at {f:me|me}.{p}

"...However, {c}{f:|}."
Kazama fixed {f:me|me} with a challenging stare and murmured slowly.
"There is just one way you can be saved.
And that is...
to keep this charm on your person.
As a special favor, I'll sell it to you for a thousand yen."{p}

......
In Kazama's hand as he said this was an eraser, the kind they sell everywhere for about fifty yen.
"...Um."
{f:I|I} began to feel that something was off.{p}

"Hm, what is it?
You'll buy it?"
Kazama's expression had changed completely from a moment ago; now he was grinning.
...Something's fishy {f:here|here}.
"Um...
...Isn't that just an ordinary eraser?"
When {f:I|I} asked, Kazama threw out his arms theatrically and rattled this off in one breath.{p}

"How dare you say such a thing you this eraser is a genuine charm that really works because I purified it myself in natural water flowing down a certain mountain famed for its miraculous powers"
While {f:I|I} was still reeling, he piled on even more.
"The mountain water I purified this eraser with comes from a waterfall that many practitioners stand under for their ascetic training.
If you purify something in that water for one night, even an ordinary eraser takes on spiritual power and becomes a charm.
You can choose anything you like to purify and turn into a charm.
It can be something you wear every day, or a key chain, or whatever.
What matters is purifying it in the water of that waterfall.
I chose an eraser because it's easy to bring to school.{p}

You know, it's a real ordeal getting to where that waterfall is.
Normally, letting it go for a thousand yen would be unthinkable.
I heard we'd be telling ghost stories about the seven wonders this time, so I brought one along in case something bad happened.{p}And I'm saying I'll part with it, specially for you."
I believe him
I don't believe him

"Kazama, I'm very sorry.
I doubted you, and I called your charm just an eraser..."
When I apologized, Kazama handed {f:me|me} the eraser and said that as long as I understood, it was fine.
So {f:I|I} thanked him and handed Kazama a thousand-yen bill.{p}

"Heh heh.
You're so obedient.
Good kid.
You really are a good kid."
Kazama gave a little "Heh heh" laugh.
...Wait, isn't something weird about this after {f:all|all}?
But it was already too late.
Kazama stuffed the bill into his pocket and hurried away from {f:me|me}.
Wh-what a guy.
All that talk about summoning the real Kokkuri-san, and showing it to us, and putting a curse on me... wasn't it all just to trick and scare {f:me|me} into buying an eraser{f:?|?}
......
Hino, why on earth did you invite someone like this...?
Oh...{p}

"I'd gone to the trouble of planning to show you the real Kokkuri-san, but now that the ritual paper has fallen, I can't do it anymore.
If you try to summon it with paper that's fallen, Kokkuri-san gets angry, you see.
Oh well, looks like all we can do is hear the next person's story.
So, whose turn is it next?"{p}

"Kazama..."
{f:I|I} was completely fed up.
Everything he said was way too fishy.
"...That's enough.
Let's hear the next person's story."
At that, Kazama started muttering.{p}

"Are you sure?
Are you really sure?
You'll get cursed, you know?
Oh, I'll even take five hundred yen, so come on, buy this charm."
...This was getting fishier and fishier.
As {f:I|I} glared at him, Kazama hurriedly started saying this.{p}

"W-well, it can't be helped.
And here I was, kindly offering to let you have the charm.
If you get into some kind of accident from now on, don't come crying to me.
Still, it's a shame.
I was planning to show you the real Kokkuri-san, but now that the ritual paper has fallen, it's no good.
If you used fallen paper, Kokkuri-san would get angry, you see.
Oh well, looks like all we can do is hear the next person's story..."
For a moment, {f:I|I} felt a chill.{p}

Come to think of it, why did the Kokkuri-san paper fall to the floor earlier, {f:I wonder|I wonder}?
Thinking back, I was sure neither Kazama nor {f:I|I} had touched it...
Kazama was fishy, but maybe some kind of spiritual presence really had come into this room.
Breaking into a cold sweat inside, {f:I|I} called out to everyone.
"W-well then, let's move on to the next story..."{p}

Well, it seems that when ordinary people do Kokkuri-san the wrong way, they can end up possessed by a low-level spirit or something.
But a Kokkuri-san researcher of my caliber has looked into all sorts of things.
I know a way to summon a high-level spirit as Kokkuri-san without fail.
So it's fine.
Leave it to me and nothing will go wrong.
Got it?
All right, let's begin.
Listen, if you want to summon the real, high-level spirit Kokkuri-san, you can't be cheap and use a ten-yen coin.
...That's right, you use a 500-yen coin.
That way you can call a better Kokkuri-san.{p}

What are you doing?
Hurry up and take out the 500-yen coin.
...Don't tell me you're not going to?
Unbelievable.{p}

You'll never get a chance like this again, you know.
Here I am, offering to summon the real, high-level Kokkuri-san for you.{p}
Are you really serious about doing this interview?
Give him a 500-yen coin
Don't give him a 500-yen coin
Say I don't have one on me

...Good, that's more like it.
Now then, let's summon Kokkuri-san with this 500-yen coin.{p}

{f:Listen|I'll say this just once more}, {f:I'll say this just once more|take out a 500-yen coin}.
{f:Take out a 500-yen coin|Refuse, and you'll be sorry}.{p}{f:If you refuse...|Do you know what that means?} {f:you'll be sorry.|Heh heh heh...}
Do as he says
Don't do as he says
...I see you've come around.{p}

Well, if you don't have one, it can't be helped.
Then let's try it with the ten-yen coin I've got on me.
But with a ten-yen coin, there's no guarantee it'll work.
All right, let's start Kokkuri-san.
{c}{f:|}, would you put your index finger on that ten-yen coin?
Here we go.{p}

...Kokkuri-san, Kokkuri-san, please come to us.
Please come into this ten-yen coin.{p}

Fundaradatta, fundaradatta, fundaradatta, kwaaaah!
......{p}

Kokkuri-san has arrived.
Now let's begin the fortune-telling.{p}So, which will it be?
Love trouble
Money trouble
Studies or work
My future

Waaaaah! K-Kokkuri-san, I'm terribly sorry!☆
A t-ten-yen coin won't do, will it!
I-I understand, please depart...!
...........................................................{p}

{c}{f:|}, this is no good.
Just as I thought, a ten-yen coin won't do.
A high-level spirit Kokkuri-san did come just now, but...
it was most displeased that we performed the ritual with a makeshift ten-yen coin.
It's no use.
We can't try any more with a ten-yen coin.
If only we had a 500-yen coin, I could have divined that question for you for sure...
Are you really sure you don't have a 500-yen coin?
Try looking one more time.{p}If you have one, I'll divine it for you right away...
Take out the 500-yen coin I was hiding
Don't take it out

"I refuse."
When {f:I|I} said that...

Kazama went into a sulk.
"Kazama?"
Even when I called to him, he wouldn't answer.
"Um, Kazama?"
"......"
"I'd like to move things along."
"......"
"Well, it can't be helped.
In that case, let's hear the next person's..."
When I tried to move on, Kazama silently tugged at {f:my|my} clothes.
...What is {f:with|with} this guy?
"P-please let go."
Kazama was looking at {f:me|me} with sad eyes.
...Oh, brother.{p}At this rate, {f:this|this} is going {f:nowhere|nowhere}.
Give in and give him a 500-yen coin
Still refuse to give him money

{f:I|I} couldn't go along with his demand.
"I'm sorry, Kazama.
I really don't have a 500-yen coin.
Please save Kokkuri-san for another time."
When {f:I|I} said that, Kazama's shoulders slumped.
Then he said just one thing.{p}

"{f:You don't even have a measly five hundred yen?|And here I was going to divine your fortune for you.} {f:You'll never be popular with girls like that.|Now I won't forgive you unless you go on a date with me.}"
...Wh-what is {f:with|with} this guy?!★{p}

"Still, it's a shame, {c}{f:|}.
If only you'd had a 500-yen coin, I could have shown you the real Kokkuri-san and divined your fortune.
And I'd prepared such good material, too.
Oops, I shouldn't call a high-level spirit Kokkuri-san 'material.'
Naughty, naughty, mutter mutter mutter..."
Kazama kept muttering to himself.
He sure is a weird {f:guy|guy}.
{f:I|I} decided to just go ahead and hear the next story,
praying that the Kokkuri-san we'd just done wasn't just one of Kazama's hoaxes.
"Well then, let's move on.
The next story is..."{p}

Why, it was an {f:eraser|eraser}.
One from the newspaper club's {f:supplies|supplies}.
......
{f:It couldn't be the work of a spirit... could it?|It isn't the work of a spirit, is it?}{p}

I had a feeling it had come flying from the direction where Kazama {f:was|was}.
{f:But|But} I couldn't exactly go and check.
Honestly, this is so {f:annoying|annoying}.
What kind of Kokkuri-san had Kazama meant to do with a 500-yen coin, {f:I wonder|I wonder}?
He'd said something about showing us the real Kokkuri-san{f:, but|, but}...
...Oh, {f:whatever|whatever}.
Kazama's kind of weird anyway, and if he did Kokkuri-san, we'd probably end up cursed {f:for real|for real}.
{f:I|I} decided to just go on and hear the next story.
"Well then, the next story..."{p}

I see, there's no one.
Then... let's see, I'll ask whether you'll meet someone to fall in love with soon.
Kokkuri-san, Kokkuri-san, please answer us.
In the near future, will a romantic encounter come {f:his|her} way?{p}

Kokkuri-san, Kokkuri-san, please answer us.
What feelings will this sweetheart come to have for {c}{f:|}?{p}
Well then, what shall I divine next?{p}

Well, well, well.
Mm-hm, mm-hm.{p}

{f:Be happy, now|Let's be happy together}.
So, what shall I divine next?{p}

We already divined that one.
Ask about something else.{p}

I see, so it's one-sided.
That's rough.
All right, this is exactly when you need Kokkuri-san.
Kokkuri-san, Kokkuri-san, please answer us.
Will {c}{f:|}'s love bear fruit?{p}
